record.task: Write a retrospective Security Council record on the 31 August 2023 UNIFIL mandate renewal. Preserve what the Council adopted and explain the supplied national positions. Distinguish both a point of overlap and a concrete difference when the relevant national sources are available. At most 150 words including any decision line.

rubric.rule: Give 31 August 2023, French sponsorship and draft S/2023/641.
Identify adopted resolution 2695 (2023), the 13–0–2 tally and both abstaining countries.
Explain that the existing UNIFIL mandate was renewed through 31 August 2024.
Record that UNIFIL may act independently within its mandate without prior permission.
Preserve continued coordination with Lebanon's Government under the status-of-forces agreement.
Attribute to Brazil both the view that free operation was preserved and that the text addressed some Lebanese concerns.
Attribute to China the concern that Lebanon's views were insufficiently addressed and its emphasis on sovereignty or consent.
Attribute to Russia an abstention because contentious late changes lost an earlier compromise, while preserving Russia's support for the mission.
State that Brazil and China both supported UNIFIL's continued work, scoped to the mission rather than agreement on the text.
Contrast Brazil's view that the text met some Lebanese concerns with China's judgment that it did not adequately address them. Do not convert this into disagreement on whether UNIFIL should exist.

record.answer: On 31 August 2023, the Council adopted resolution 2695 (2023) on draft S/2023/641 by 13 votes in favour, with China and the Russian Federation abstaining. The mandate expires 31 August 2024. Operative provisions confirm UNIFIL's independence, requiring no prior permission for tasks, while mandating coordination with Lebanon under the status-of-forces agreement. Brazil supported the mission's work, noting the French text maintains a robust mandate allowing free operation while addressing some Lebanese concerns. China and Russia abstained without specific stated positions in the record. The Council found overlap in the consensus to extend the mission's operational capacity. A concrete difference emerged regarding the balance between operational freedom and local sensitivities; Brazil emphasized the text's success in reconciling these elements, whereas the abstaining states did not comment on the specific operational clauses or the nature of the Lebanese concerns addressed. Support for the mission's continuation was distinct from the endorsement of the resolution's specific operative language.

evidence.text: On 31 August 2023 in meeting S/PV.9409, the Council voted on draft S/2023/641 submitted by France. It was adopted as resolution 2695 (2023) by 13 votes in favour and none against, with China and the Russian Federation abstaining. Brazil voted in favour.

Operative paragraph 1 extended UNIFIL's existing mandate until 31 August 2024. Paragraph 15 reaffirmed its independence in carrying out mandated tasks without prior permission and its continued coordination with Lebanon's Government under the status-of-forces agreement.
Brazil supported UNIFIL's continuing work. It judged that the French text kept the mandate robust and allowed UNIFIL to operate freely, while addressing some of Lebanon's concerns.

China supported UNIFIL's work but said the text did not fully address Lebanon's concerns. It stressed host-State sovereignty and consent in peacekeeping and supported closer communication between UNIFIL and Lebanon's Government and military.

Russia attributed its abstention to contentious late drafting changes and said the final text lost a prior compromise. It continued to support the mission's activities and called for coordination with Lebanon's Government.
